Problem: Find the foot of the perpendicular from the point $A = (1,8,4)$ to the line passing through $B = (0,-1,3)$ and $C = (2,-3,-1).$

message.content:
Let the line through \(B=(0,-1,3)\) and \(C=(2,-3,-1)\) have direction vector  
\[
\vec d = C-B=(2,-2,-4)=2(1,-1,-2).
\]
Using the simpler direction vector
\[
\vec d=(1,-1,-2),
\]
a point on the line is
\[
F=B+t\vec d=(0,-1,3)+t(1,-1,-2).
\]

For \(F\) to be the foot of the perpendicular from \(A=(1,8,4)\), we need
\[
(A-F)\cdot \vec d=0.
\]
Now
\[
A-B=(1,9,1).
\]
So
\[
t=\frac{(A-B)\cdot \vec d}{\vec d\cdot \vec d}
=\frac{(1,9,1)\cdot(1,-1,-2)}{(1,-1,-2)\cdot(1,-1,-2)}
=\frac{1-9-2}{1+1+4}
=\frac{-10}{6}
=-\frac{5}{3}.
\]
Thus
\[
F=(0,-1,3)-\frac{5}{3}(1,-1,-2)
=\left(-\frac{5}{3},-1+\frac{5}{3},3+\frac{10}{3}\right)
=\left(-\frac{5}{3},\frac{2}{3},\frac{19}{3}\right).
\]

The answer is \(\left(-\frac{5}{3},\frac{2}{3},\frac{19}{3}\right)\).
